ROTATIONAL DYNAMICS CLASS NOTES

Good morning students, please pay attention and remember to submit your homework by Friday.
Today we are going to look at rotational motion and some related physics things.

Torque is defined as the rotational analogue of force, given by the cross product of position vector and force vector: tau = r x F.
As you know from last week, the rate of change of...
Wait, let's write down the next concept clearly.
Moment of Inertia is the rotational mass of a rigid body, defined as the sum of mass times squared distance from the axis of rotation: I = \sum m_i r_i^2.
Also note that the thing we talked about earlier...
Angular Momentum is the rotational counterpart of linear momentum, given by L = r x p = I omega.
The Principle of Conservation of Angular Momentum states that if the net external torque acting on a system is zero, total angular momentum remains constant.
Remember this formula because it appears often in tests!
